transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Elena Vos (Redwood) — Marta Ruiz, Devon Clarke, Liu Wen, Evan Park, Asha Mehta (Aurum)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to unblock procurement/ legal for an audited healthcare POC. Focus on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS, and billing approvals.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick agenda — legal redlines, security pack, pricing and pilot SOW. can we do a quick round intro?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: sure, marta here procurement lead, i'll own intake and approvals on our side.
[00:12] Devon Clarke: devon, security arch, i'm focused on encryption, network, and KMS.
[00:16] Liu Wen: liu, legal counsel, i'll review the MSA and DPA.
[00:20] Evan Park: finops, so billing questions and committed spend.
[00:23] Asha Mehta: engineering manager, i'll coordinate with priya on the pilot.
[00:28] Priya Nair: hi all, priya, se — i'll own pilot tech run and benchmark notes.
[00:31] Jordan Lee: cool — main ask from aurum was around audited onboarding for healthcare data, right? devon, can you summarize security blockers?
[00:40] Devon Clarke: yeah — short list: 1) we need KMS integration, hardware-backed ideally, HSM or cloud KMS; 2) data residency, we need logs and tokens stored in region us-east-2; 3) audit logs and retention policy — 7 years for certain records; and 4) options for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) if we can't get contractual guarantees.
[01:05] Priya Nair: okay understood, we support KMS via customer-managed keys, we have an HSM-backed path — i'll pack the notes. just a head's up that some of the low-level naming in our docs says K V cache, uh — sorry — KV cache optimizations, that won't change key mgmt, it's separate.
[01:22] Evan Park: on billing, quick question: finance won't sign until we see committed pricing vs purely usage model. can you show committed discounts and overage caps?
[01:31] Jordan Lee: absolutely — we can do committed capacity (dedicated) pricing and a hosted API usage comparison. i'll share a pricing workbook with tiered committed scenarios and an estimate for token throughput and unit economics.
[01:42] Liu Wen: on the DPA, we have three hot spots: sub-processor list and liability cap, right to audit language, and data deletion/retention windows. our security team also flagged breach notification timing.
[01:55] Elena Vos: for the audit clause we typically provide SOC 2 Type II report and if needed we can do a read-only audit for specific scopes; for sub-processors we can provide a current list and agree to 30 days notice on changes. breach notification we do 72 hours for incidents with PII exposure, typical language in our DPA.
[02:15] Devon Clarke: is the 72 hours contractual? we need it in writing, and also MFA plus SAML SSO for admin console, RBAC for token generation.
[02:26] Priya Nair: yes, we support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC on the console, and MFA on admin accounts. i'll include screenshots in the security pack.
[02:36] Marta Ruiz: procurement timeline — we have a gating committee next week, so any legal redlines need to be in by EOD next Friday to hit the next funding window.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: understood — we'll prioritize MSA/DPA redline summary and security pack to meet that date.
[02:51] Evan Park: about dedicated vs hosted — performance is key for our real time summarization workloads. do you have latency SLOs? and what happens when capacity is constrained?
[03:05] Priya Nair: our hosted offering has SLOs we publish per model and region, typically p95 token latency in the 200–400ms range depending on model and seq length. dedicated gives you reserved throughput and lower variance. we also support smart routing and fallback to a compatible variant if a specific instance becomes saturated.
[03:22] Asha Mehta: can we get an SLA with credits if you miss latency targets? that's a common ask for platform teams.
[03:29] Jordan Lee: yes, for dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime/latency commitments and credits; for hosted it's standard SLOs and escalation paths. legal can review the exact credit formula.
[03:38] Liu Wen: liability cap — we need it to be at least twice of the committed fees for the first year, otherwise it's a blocker. is that negotiable?
[03:46] Elena Vos: we can discuss adjustments; typically we tie caps to a multiple of fees, and for enterprise deals we can expand liability for specific security exceptions. i'll put a few options in the redline memo.
[03:58] Devon Clarke: one more — data residency. aurum requires customer data to remain in region, including backups. can you guarantee that for hosted?
[04:07] Priya Nair: for hosted we can pin workloads to regions and ensure primary and backups in-region for certain plans; dedicated and private deployments give stronger guarantees. i'll document region pinning constraints and operational playbooks.
[04:20] Evan Park: on cost — FinOps wants a clear estimate for the pilot: expected tokens per month, peak qps, and recommended quantization/packing settings to reduce cost.
[04:33] Priya Nair: we can provide a pilot SOW with expected throughput and suggested quant profiles; note that quantization options vary by model architecture and can affect quality slightly, we'll include recommended tradeoffs.
[04:48] Jordan Lee: can we agree on pilot success metrics now? say: 1) end-to-end latency under X ms for 95p under pilot load, 2) cost per 1k tokens under threshold, 3) no critical security exceptions in audit.
[05:02] Asha Mehta: yep that's reasonable. engineering needs the exact request pattern for the benchmark — we'll provide sample traffic next 48 hours.
[05:10] Samir Patel: i'll handle onboarding and SSO test plan once we get confirmation of environment.
[05:15] Marta Ruiz: legal gating: if redlines are material we escalate to our counsel, which adds a two-week delay. can redlines be summarized as alternatives to minimize back-and-forth?
[05:26] Elena Vos: yes i'll produce a redline summary with proposed language plus alternative clauses we can accept. that should shorten negotiation cycles.
[05:35] Liu Wen: also need to confirm data deletion API and proof of deletion for PHI.
[05:41] Priya Nair: we expose data deletion endpoints and audit logs for deletion actions; for PHI we recommend dedicated deployment with stricter isolation — i'll detail processes and proof artifacts in the pack.
[05:53] Devon Clarke: what about export controls and cross-border transfers? we need assurances we don't route through jurisdictions that cause regulatory issues.
[06:01] Elena Vos: we'll include geo routing and subprocessor list and will confirm no routed processing through restricted regions.
[06:08] Evan Park: timeline question again: if you deliver docs by next tuesday, does that get us ready for procurement gating next Friday?
[06:16] Jordan Lee: yes, our internal target: price workbook by Thu, security pack Mon/Tue, redline memo by next Tuesday, that should align.
[06:25] Marta Ruiz: great. a few nitpicks from procurement: invoicing cadence — monthly vs annual prepay — and tax flow.
[06:34] Jordan Lee: we have flexible invoicing: monthly usage billing, annual prepay with discount, and committed monthly billing for Dedicated. i'll outline tax and billing flows in the worksheet.
[06:44] Evan Park: what about support SLAs — response times for Sev1/Sev2?
[06:49] Samir Patel: enterprise support tiers include 15-minute Sev1 response and a named CSM; standard has longer windows. we'll include response SLAs per tier.
[06:58] Liu Wen: curious on indemnification for PHI exposures — does your MSA accept contractual indemnity for breaches caused by vendor negligence?
[07:05] Elena Vos: we have indemnity clauses and we'll map them to the relevant data processing obligations; we'll flag any exposure areas in the redline doc.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: ok wrapping. agreed deliverables and deadlines listed in action items. any final questions?
[07:19] Marta Ruiz: please include a one-page summary for our committee with clear pros/cons hosted vs dedicated and a recommended path for a pilot.
[07:27] Jordan Lee: yes, will do. thanks everyone.
[07:30] Meeting close.

--- End Transcript ---
